(1) the Gricean Maxims are a useful tool for adapting data analysis algorithms to communicate effectively with users, (2) the Griceans Maxims can be applied to time series data, and (3) the Griceians Maxims are a key element of generating English summaries of time-series.
(a) Grice's maxims are useful for guiding the selection of information to communicate to a human user, and (b) the maxims can be applied by modifying standard data analysis algorithms.

(a) we have developed a system for generating textual summaries of time series, which is operational in the meteorological domain, (b) we can use the Gricean principles of cooperative communication to modify data analysis algorithms in order to produce more effective summaries, (c) we can use a combination of Gricean principles to produce summaries which are more effective than summaries produced using only one principle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: How should a computer system generate textual summaries of data for human users?
developing a general methodology for generating textual summaries of data, which we call the Data-to-Text (D2T) methodology.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Gricean Maxims are useful for designing data analysis algorithms that communicate information to human users.
data analysis algorithms can be modified to communicate the information that is most relevant to human users, by applying the Gricean principles of cooperative discourse.
